title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 4
summary: Oil headed for its biggest weekly gain since July as renewed US-Iran hostilities heightened concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Hong Kong’s Picky IPO Issuers Rewrite Playbook for Allocations
summary: Hong Kong’s boom in initial public offerings has turned getting shares in the hottest deals into something of an invitation-only affair.

title: Anthropic Nears Finalizing $15 Billion Pre-IPO Credit Facility
summary: Anthropic PBC is set to finalize expanding its revolving credit facility to $15 billion, according to people familiar with the matter, clearing a hurdle before the artificial intelligence firm’s public filing for its highly anticipated IPO.

title: SEC Moves to Nix Rule on Adviser Political Donations
summary: Investment advisers would no longer be prohibited from offering services to public pension funds if they made recent political donations to state and local elected officials, the Securities and Exchange Commission said in a proposed rule change Thursday.

title: Asia Stocks to Gain as Fed Bets Cool, Dollar Drops: Markets Wrap
summary: Stocks in Asia were poised to rise Friday, tracking gains on Wall Street as investors pared bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike this month. The yen held its biggest gain in over a month and oil rose.

title: Stocks Climb as Fed-Hike Wagers Ease on Waller: Markets Wrap
summary: Stocks rose the most in a month as Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he’d be willing to support holding rates steady if price pressures continue to show signs of easing.

title: Lululemon Needs a Full Product Overhaul, Widlitz Says
summary: SW Retail Advisors President and founder Stacey Widlitz discusses Lululemon Athletica lowering its full-year outlook for a second straight quarter on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Yen Rises as Intervention, BOJ Rate Hike Risks Jolt Traders
summary: The yen strengthened nearly 2% Thursday, reversing a month of gradual decline, as traders lifted bets on Bank of Japan interest-rate hikes and remained vigilant to the risk of official action to further boost the currency.

title: Wine Distributor Stephen Burton Gets Prison Term in Rare Vintage Scam
summary: The founder of a London wine-distribution business was sentenced in the US to six years in prison for orchestrating a scam that cost investors almost $100 million and was based on bottles of rare vintages that didn’t exist.

title: Toyota’s Sato on How Japanese Automakers Stay Relevant
summary: Toyota Vice Chairman and Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association Chairman Koji Sato sits down for an exclusive Bloomberg Television interview with Shery Ahn to discuss how Japanese automakers can stay relevant globally, as well as Toyota's hydrogen business. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: The Hottest New Trade Is Your Own Electricity
summary:
Could the hottest new trade be your own electricity? Zero host Akshat Rathi meets the vibe coders making money from their excess energy. Listen to the Big Take podcast.

 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Australia’s Battered Bonds Have Reasons to Rebound, Funds Say
summary: Australia’s bonds, caught up in the global fixed-income selloff, have seen their yields rise more than any of their peers in the past month, despite arguments that the country’s finances are in much better shape.

title: S&P 500 Notches Best Day in Month as Traders Pare Rate-Hike Bets
summary: The S&P 500 Index clocked its best day in a month on Thursday as investors weighed remarks from Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller, who offered optimism that inflation is showing some signs of slowing. Traders accordingly pared bets for interest-rate hikes in September.

title: Bessent 'Wants To Win', Drive Yields Lower: Brill
summary:
Matt Brill, head of North American investment grade credit at Invesco, and Meghan Robson, head of US credit strategy at BNP Paribas, joins Michael McKee on "Bloomberg Real Yield." They discuss Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's focus on driving yields lower.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: IMF Mulls Opening Caracas Office as Venezuela Engagement Deepens
summary: The International Monetary Fund is considering opening a local office in Venezuela, establishing permanent representation in the country for the first time in years, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: UBS's Panseri on Global Bond Yields, ECB Hike Expectations
summary: UBS Wealth Management France CIO Claudia Panseri discusses the Yen as global bond yields surged on inflation concerns. She speaks with Lizzy Burden on Bloomberg TV. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Behind the Making of the US Open's Famous Honey Deuce Cocktail
summary: Aleco Azqueta, global VP of Marketing for Grey Goose at Bacardi, said that he loves that tennis fans get to take home a bit of US Open history when they buy an iconic Honey Deuce drink (and cup) at the tournament. Azqueta said that the drink has grown to be part of the 'center' of the US Open and creates 'moment of connection' for visitors.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Lei Qiu Says AI Is Moving Into Adoption Phase
summary: AllianceBernstein's Thematic Innovation Equities Chief investment Officer Lei Qiu says the latest earnings reports point to strong and persistent AI demand. He argues there is clear evidence of AI adoption broadening beyond hardware into select software and the infrastructure layer, showing that AI is becoming more integrated into business models. In Qiu's view, AI is solidly moving into the adoption phase, with no sign of a slowdown. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Cash-Strapped Colleges Are Draining Their Endowments to Survive
summary: Bloomberg's Amanda Albright joins Michael McKee on "Bloomberg Real Yield." Nearly 200 private colleges are draining their endowments to stay alive as they face financial pressure due to declining enrollments and shrinking income. (Source: Bloomberg)
